page: Amazon Web Services m8g.xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. It features 4 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1D cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance runs on the Nitro hypervisor, has a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities across most general computing tasks. The server demonstrates average performance in stress-ng single-core (1707.29) and multi-core (6818.16) tests, as well as in Geekbench single-core (1802.0) and multi-core (5846.0) evaluations. Memory bandwidth is solid, reaching 462.02 GB/sec for cached read-only small blocks and 96.39 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is a relative strength, placing in the top 25% with 14.17 GB/sec. However, the server exhibits weaknesses in Passmark CPU scores (3953.8) and extended instructions, with a poor showing in the Passmark CPU encryption test (753.29). LLM inference speeds are also weak, yielding 72.27 tokens/sec for text generation on a small 135M model and 6.51 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8g.xlarge offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads without the premium of specialized hardware. The absence of local storage and GPU accelerators makes it a streamlined option for workloads that rely on network-attached storage and standard CPU execution. Given its benchmark profile, this server is well-suited for applications such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 10.08 GB/sec, Redis database operations (9.39 million SET operations/sec), software compilation, and general-purpose text or image processing. It is less suitable for heavy cryptographic operations or large-scale machine learning inference.
